owner.name: Maren Voss
owner.heading: How Huckleberry started
owner.bio: Maren Voss was the seventh number in every group text that started with "this is so last minute, but…". A mom of three in Star, she was the neighbor who always knew a sitter — until knowing one wasn't enough, and she started matching them to families on purpose. Huckleberry Sitters is that habit, grown up: a small circle of sitters she'd trust with her own three, a meet-and-greet before any booking, and evenings that run on your family's routine instead of a stranger's guesswork.

faq.a: No — and that's on purpose. We're the babysitter: one family at a time, in your own home, on your schedule. We don't run a facility, we don't do all-day group care, and your kids never leave the house. If you need full-time weekday care, a daycare is the right tool — we're the evenings-and-in-between people.

faq.q: Do we meet the sitter before we book?
faq.a: Always. Every new family starts with a meet-and-greet — the sitter comes by, the kids size them up, you ask everything you want to ask. You book a sitter after you've met them, never before.

People we know personally, not names from an app. Every sitter starts as someone from our own circle here in Star, and every family meets them before booking. If the fit isn't right, we'll suggest someone else — no hard feelings.

The base rate covers one kid; each additional kid and weekend evenings add a little. The exact math is in the rates section, and the planner above estimates it for your crew. We confirm the final rate together before your first booking.
You write the routine, we run it — bath nights, teeth, which stuffed animal is the right one, how far the door stays open. Kids do best with their own routine, so we don't improvise a new one.

A dog that needs letting out, a cat that needs ignoring — tap "Pet-friendly sitter" in the planner and we'll match you with someone comfortable around animals. For pets with special handling, leave notes like you would for the kids.
Text us. Evenings can be rebooked or cancelled without drama — we'd rather keep your trust than charge you for a night that didn't happen.

services.title: Date Night
services.desc: An evening out without the group-text scramble. Your sitter arrives before you leave, runs the routine you set, and sends you out the door unhurried.

services.title: After School
services.desc: Pickup-time to parent-time coverage — snacks, homework minutes, and backyard energy burned off before dinner.

services.title: Occasional Daytime
services.desc: Work-from-home crunch days, appointments, a morning to yourself — daytime hours booked by the block, no weekly commitment.

services.title: Mother's Helper
services.desc: An extra pair of hands while you're home — new-baby weeks, big-family evenings, party prep. You stay in charge; we keep the little ones busy.

rundown.desc: Your sitter arrives ten minutes early for the handoff — house notes, allergies, routines, and where the snacks live.
Shoes off, coats up, and straight into whatever your kids are into — blocks, backyard, board games. Screens follow your house rules; we default to off.
Backpacks open before the fun stuff. Your sitter sits with them through worksheets and reading minutes — encouraging, not doing it for them.
Something simple and kid-approved — mac and cheese, quesadillas, whatever you've left in the fridge with instructions.
Toys back in bins, dishes in the dishwasher, kitchen wiped down. You come home to the house you left.
Dog let out, water bowls topped up, cat left to supervise from the stairs. Sitters comfortable around animals, matched on request.
Lights lower, voices lower — a book pile and quiet play so bedtime doesn't arrive as a surprise.
Your routine, run your way — bath if it's a bath night, teeth, one more book (just one), and the door left open the exact right amount.
What they ate, what they played, how bedtime landed — waiting for you in a quick note when you walk in.
